answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a vouching ridge: a new identity may only earn after three established agents stake part of their own standing on it, like a trellis that holds up only vines it is tied to. If the newcomer cheats, its vouchers lose standing too, so no established agent vouches for strangers lightly. A farm must therefore corrupt real, reputable nodes one by one, and its fake identities cluster in the sable corners of the graph where no voucher reaches, visible, isolated, and cheap to cut off, while one honest agent needs only three genuine vouches.
